unit.label: Descriptions & weekends
unit.title: What Shall We Do This Weekend?
unit.description: 10 new words and activities. Describe, share hobbies, and make a weekend plan.
unit.bookReference: Book 1 · Lessons 2–3: descriptions, hobbies & weekend plans

lessons.title: People and Photos
lessons.subtitle: Ask how many and describe someone

steps.prompt: Which sentence describes how the photo looks?
steps.explanation: 很好看 describes its appearance. The other sentences identify its owner or count photos.
Use 沒有 as the negative of 有.

lessons.title: At the Weekend
lessons.subtitle: Put a time before an activity

steps.prompt: Which sentence puts the time after “I”?
steps.explanation: Both time positions are natural. This question specifically asks for subject, then time, then activity.
You already know 什麼: what.

lessons.title: Go Swimming
lessons.subtitle: Add one activity and say where the plan leads

steps.prompt: What does 去 add in 我去游泳?
options: Going somewhere to do the activity
steps.answer: Going somewhere to do the activity
steps.explanation: 去 means go; 游泳 says what you go to do.

steps.prompt: Which visible component is on the left of 泳?
steps.explanation: 泳 has three water strokes on the left and 永 on the right.

lessons.title: What Do You Do Often?
lessons.subtitle: Use a familiar activity in a new pattern

steps.prompt: Your friend likes swimming. Say you like it too.
steps.explanation: 也 adds a matching preference. 常 says how often an activity happens.
都 includes everyone in 我們.

lessons.title: Make a Suggestion
lessons.subtitle: Use 吧 to propose a shared activity

steps.prompt: 要不要 is a question about…
steps.explanation: The positive–negative question pattern asks whether the listener wants it.

steps.prompt: Your friend says 我們去游泳吧. What are they doing?
steps.explanation: Sentence-final 吧 makes this a friendly “Let’s…” suggestion.

steps.prompt: Which component is on the right of 吧?
steps.explanation: 吧 places 口 beside 巴. You have also seen 巴 inside 爸.

lessons.title: Unit 7 Review
lessons.subtitle: Describe, share a hobby, and suggest a plan

steps.prompt: A: 你週末做什麼？ B: 我去游泳。 What does B do?
options: Asks how many teachers there are
steps.explanation: The question supplies the time 週末; the reply gives the activity.

steps.prompt: A: 她喜歡看電影。 B: 我也喜歡看電影。 What do they share?
steps.explanation: 也 adds the second speaker’s matching preference.

幾.note: 幾 asks for a number. In 幾個, it takes the place of the number before the classifier.
幾.memory: Two small 幺 shapes sit side by side at the top of 幾. Below them, notice the crossing diagonals and the long hooked stroke.

parts.label: 幺幺
parts.name: paired upper shapes
parts.description: The first six strokes make two compact 幺 shapes: keep each small enough to fit beside the other.

parts.label: lower
parts.name: crossing lower strokes
parts.description: The last six strokes include the lower crossing slants and a long hooked stroke that starts between the upper shapes. Follow their order in the animation.

老.meaning: old; first syllable of 老師
老.note: 老師 (lǎoshī) means teacher. 老 places 耂 above 匕. A long slant cuts down through the upper horizontal strokes; the hooked lower shape tucks underneath.
老.memory: 老 places 耂 above 匕. A long slant cuts down through the upper horizontal strokes; the hooked lower shape tucks underneath.

parts.label: 耂
parts.name: 耂 component
parts.description: The first four strokes form the upper group: horizontal, vertical, another horizontal, then the long downward-left slant.

parts.label: 匕
parts.name: 匕 component
parts.description: The final two strokes form the compact hooked shape below. Keep it tucked under the spreading upper group.

師.note: 師 first appears in 老師 (lǎoshī), teacher. Recognize its shape while learning 老師 as one word.
師.memory: Remember 師 by its two stacked spaces on the left and a hanging 巾 shape under a bar on the right.

parts.label: 𠂤
parts.name: left group
parts.description: 𠂤 forms the left side, with a short top slant and two stacked, box-like spaces.

parts.label: 帀
parts.name: right group
parts.description: 帀 is a horizontal bar above 巾; its central vertical extends down through the hanging frame.

相.note: In 照相, read 相 as xiàng, with a fourth tone. Learn 照相 as the whole activity: taking photos.
相.memory: 相 places 木 beside 目. Recognize a tree-shaped left side and an eye-shaped rectangle with two inner lines.

parts.label: 木
parts.name: tree-shaped left side
parts.description: 木 takes the first four strokes on the left. Its final stroke becomes compact to make room for 目.

parts.label: 目
parts.name: eye-shaped right side
parts.description: 目 is the tall rectangle on the right with two short horizontal lines inside it.

電.note: 電影 (diànyǐng) means movie. 電 stacks the rain component 雨 over a lower box with a long hooked stroke. The final hook reaches down and curls to the right.
電.memory: 電 stacks the rain component 雨 over a lower box with a long hooked stroke. The final hook reaches down and curls to the right.

parts.label: 雨
parts.name: 雨 component
parts.description: The eight upper strokes form the rain component, including its small internal marks beneath the cover.

parts.label: lower
parts.name: lower group
parts.description: The lower five strokes include the box-like middle and the long final hook. Keep the hook free to extend below the upper part.

影.note: 電影 (diànyǐng) means movie. 影 places 景 beside three slanting strokes 彡. On the left, 景 stacks 日 over 京; on the right, keep the three slants clearly separated.
影.memory: 影 places 景 beside three slanting strokes 彡. On the left, 景 stacks 日 over 京; on the right, keep the three slants clearly separated.

parts.label: 景
parts.name: 景 component
parts.description: The twelve strokes of 景 occupy the left side. Look for the upper 日 and the smaller stacked shapes below it.

parts.label: 彡
parts.name: 彡 component
parts.description: Three separate downward-left slants run along the right edge, with the lowest stroke reaching furthest down.

週.note: 週末 (zhōumò) means weekend. 週 wraps the movement component 辶 around 周. Write the inner 周 first, then finish the path that runs along its left and underneath it.
週.memory: 週 wraps the movement component 辶 around 周. Write the inner 周 first, then finish the path that runs along its left and underneath it.

parts.label: 周
parts.name: 周 component
parts.description: 周 is the enclosed inner component. Its upper and lower internal strokes fit inside the surrounding outline.

parts.label: 辶
parts.name: 辶 component
parts.description: The Taiwan form here has four strokes in the movement component. Its final long stroke sweeps beneath 周.

週.partOrderLabel: inside first, then the surrounding movement component

末.note: 末 means end in 週末: the end of the week, or weekend.
末.memory: For 末, the TOP horizontal is longer than the horizontal below it. A vertical runs through both, with two sloping strokes spreading below.

parts.label: 末
parts.name: long top bar and spreading base
parts.description: Notice the long first horizontal, shorter second horizontal, central vertical, and two spreading final strokes. The long top bar identifies 末.

做.note: 做什麼 (zuò shénme) means do what. 做 has three visible columns: the person component 亻, 古 in the middle, and 攵 on the right. 古 itself is 十 above 口.
做.memory: 做 has three visible columns: the person component 亻, 古 in the middle, and 攵 on the right. 古 itself is 十 above 口.

parts.label: 亻
parts.name: 亻 component
parts.description: The narrow two-stroke person component sits at the left. Keep it compact so the two groups to its right have room.

parts.label: 古
parts.name: 古 component
parts.description: 古 forms the middle column: a cross above a small mouth-shaped box. These five strokes come before the right component.

parts.label: 攵
parts.name: 攵 component
parts.description: The final four strokes make the right-hand component. Its two longer diagonal strokes cross and spread outward.

游.note: 游泳 (yóuyǒng) means swim. 游 has 氵 at the left, 方 in the middle, and a small two-stroke top above 子 on the right. Do not confuse its right side with 永 in 泳.
游.memory: 游 has 氵 at the left, 方 in the middle, and a small two-stroke top above 子 on the right. Do not confuse its right side with 永 in 泳.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: 氵 component
parts.description: The first three strokes make the water component, a useful meaning clue for swimming.

parts.label: 方
parts.name: 方 component
parts.description: 方 occupies the middle column. Leave space to its right for the small top strokes and 子.

parts.label: right
parts.name: right-hand group
parts.description: The final five strokes form a two-stroke cap above 子. Notice the separate child-shaped group at the lower right.

泳.note: 泳 completes 游泳, to swim. Its water component helps you remember the activity.
泳.memory: 泳 is 氵 + 永. Put three water strokes on the left and the branching 永 shape on the right.

parts.label: 氵
parts.name: water component
parts.description: The three strokes of 氵 sit along the left edge. Water is a useful meaning clue for swimming.

parts.label: 永
parts.name: right-hand sound component
parts.description: 永 suggests the yong syllable. Its central hooked stroke is surrounded by spreading side strokes; 泳 has a third tone.

常.note: 常 means often. Put it before the activity, as in 常看電影.
常.memory: 常 stacks a small spreading top, a cover and 口 above 巾. The final vertical descends through the lower hanging shape.

parts.label: 尚
parts.name: upper group
parts.description: The upper eight strokes contain three small top strokes, a cover, and a 口 underneath that cover.

parts.label: 巾
parts.name: lower hanging shape
parts.description: 巾 forms the lower three strokes. Its final vertical runs down through the middle of the hanging outline.

吧.note: At the end of 我們去看電影吧, 吧 makes a friendly suggestion. Say ba lightly, without a tone mark.
吧.memory: 吧 is 口 + 巴. The small mouth on the left sits beside the hooked 巴 shape you saw under 爸.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: mouth component
parts.description: 口 occupies the first three strokes on the left, a useful clue for a particle used in speech.

parts.label: 巴
parts.name: right-hand component
parts.description: 巴 occupies the right side. Notice its upper enclosed space and the rounded hook below, also seen in 爸.

u7-count.title: Ask for the number
u7-count.explanation: You already know 有, 沒有, 個 and 兩. 幾 (jǐ) asks “how many” when a fairly small number is expected. Replace the number with 幾; keep 個 and the noun in place. In 你家有幾個人, 家 refers to the family/household and 人 to its members. Answer by replacing 幾 with a number you know. 幾 already makes this a question, so do not add 嗎.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ ge rén?
examples.meaning: How many people are in your family?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu liǎng ge rén.
examples.meaning: There are two people in my family.

u7-count.remember: Use 兩個 for two. In these counting phrases, 個 is often pronounced lightly as ge.

u7-photo-hobby.title: From a photo to taking photos
u7-photo-hobby.explanation: 照片 (zhàopiàn) is a thing: a photo. 照相 (zhàoxiàng) is an activity: take photos. They share 照 but have different second characters and meanings. You already know 喜歡 (xǐhuān). Put the activity directly after it to say what you like doing. Use 不喜歡 for an activity you do not like.

examples.meaning: My older sister does not like taking photos.

u7-photo-hobby.remember: 照片 is the photo; 照相 is taking it. Keep the book’s xǐhuān spelling.

u7-weekend.title: Ask what happens at the weekend
u7-weekend.explanation: 週末 (zhōumò) means weekend; 做 (zuò) means do. 做什麼 means do what. A time word normally goes after the subject and before the activity: 你週末做什麼？ It can also go before the subject: 週末你做什麼？ Both are natural. 什麼 stays where the unknown activity belongs, and you do not add 嗎.

examples.meaning: What do you do at the weekend?
At the weekend, I take photos.

u7-weekend.remember: Put 週末 before the activity. For the building exercises, follow the requested time-word position.

u7-go.title: Go and do an activity
u7-go.explanation: You know 去, go. Put a complete activity after it to say “go do that activity”: 去游泳, go swimming; 去看電影, go see a movie. Keep the activity’s own verb. Add the time before 去 to say when. This pattern can express a plan; no English-style “to” needs an extra Chinese word.

examples.meaning: At the weekend, I go swimming.
We are going to see a movie.

u7-go.remember: 去 tells us we go; the phrase after 去 tells us what we go to do.

u7-often.title: Say what you do often
u7-often.explanation: 常 (cháng) means often: an activity happens frequently. It does not mean every time, and it is not an exact equivalent of “usually.” Put 常 before the whole activity. To say what you often do on weekends, put 週末 before 常.
u7-often.remember: Time first, then 常, then the activity.

u7-also-all.title: Old words, new activities
u7-also-all.pattern: subject + 也 / 都 + verb phrase
u7-also-all.explanation: 也 (yě), also, and 都 (dōu), all/both, are review from earlier units. Use 也 to add a matching fact in a conversation: someone likes swimming, and you do too. Use 都 with a group such as 我們 to say the statement is true of everyone in that group. Both go before 喜歡 when describing shared likes. Here 都 means all/both, not often.

examples.text: 她喜歡游泳。我也喜歡游泳。
examples.pinyin: Tā xǐhuān yóuyǒng. Wǒ yě xǐhuān yóuyǒng.
examples.meaning: She likes swimming. I like swimming too.

u7-also-all.remember: 也 adds “too”; 都 includes everyone; 常 tells how often. Practise them separately here.

u7-suggest.title: Make a friendly suggestion
u7-suggest.pattern: 我們 + 去 + activity + 吧
u7-suggest.explanation: 吧 (ba) is a light, neutral-tone particle at the end of a sentence. After 我們去 + activity, it makes a simple suggestion: “Let’s go…” The listener can accept with the familiar 好, “OK.” You know 嗎 for a yes/no question. Here 吧 proposes something to do together; it does not ask whether a statement is true.
u7-suggest.remember: Put 吧 at the very end of the suggestion and pronounce it lightly.

u7-describe.title: People and descriptions
u7-describe.explanation: 老師 (lǎoshī) means teacher. Use 是 to identify a person’s role: 她是老師. 好看 (hǎokàn) means good-looking or nice to look at. Use 很 before this description, without 是: 這張照片很好看. You already know the two sentence patterns; the new words let you say more about people and photos.

examples.meaning: My older sister is a teacher.

u7-describe.remember: A role follows 是. A simple adjective description follows 很.

u7-movies.title: From reading to watching movies
u7-movies.explanation: You know 看 from 看書, read a book. 看電影 (kàn diànyǐng) means watch movies: 電影 is movie, and 看 tells us what we do. Keep 看電影 together as one activity after 喜歡. 照相 means take photos; 看電影 means watch movies.

examples.meaning: She does not like watching movies.

u7-movies.remember: The familiar 看 takes a different object: 書 or 電影.

u7-swim.title: One more activity: swimming
u7-swim.explanation: 游泳 (yóuyǒng) means swim. These two characters make one activity; learn both together. You can put 游泳 straight after 喜歡 or 想. 我喜歡游泳 describes a general preference; 我想游泳 says what you want to do.
u7-swim.remember: 游 and 泳 both have a water component. Keep the whole word 游泳 together.

u7-family-count.pinyin: Nǐ jiā yǒu jǐ ge rén?
u7-family-count.meaning: How many people are in your family?
u7-family-count.note: 幾 takes the number’s place, directly before 個人.

u7-two-people.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǒu liǎng ge rén.
u7-two-people.meaning: There are two people in my family.
u7-two-people.note: Replace 幾 with 兩; keep the rest of the counting phrase.

u7-teacher.meaning: My older sister is a teacher.
u7-teacher.note: Reuse the natural close-family expression 我姐姐; use 是 for her role.

u7-photo-like.note: An activity can follow 喜歡 directly. 照相 is taking photos.

u7-weekend-ask.meaning: At the weekend, what do you do? Start with the time.
u7-weekend-ask.note: The time goes first in this version. 你週末做什麼 is also grammatical.

u7-weekend-photo.meaning: I take photos at the weekend. Start with “I.”
u7-weekend-photo.note: The subject comes first, then time, then activity.

u7-movies.note: 看電影 is one complete activity: watch movies.

u7-go-swim.meaning: At the weekend, I go swimming. Start with the time.
u7-go-swim.note: Time first in this version, then the subject and 去 + activity.

u7-often-movies.note: 常 belongs before the complete activity.

u7-also-swim.note: Put 也 before 喜歡, not at the end as English “too” would go.

u7-suggest-movie.note: Put 吧 at the very end to make a friendly suggestion.

u7-suggest-swim.note: The activity changes, but the suggestion pattern stays the same.

u7-sister-weekend.text: 你姐姐週末喜歡做什麼？
u7-sister-weekend.pinyin: Nǐ jiějie zhōumò xǐhuān zuò shénme?
u7-sister-weekend.meaning: What does your older sister like doing at the weekend? Start with “your older sister.”
u7-sister-weekend.note: 你姐姐 is the subject; 週末 gives the time; 喜歡做什麼 asks about the activity she likes.

u7-she-movies.note: 她 refers back to the older sister in the conversation.

u7-all-movies.pinyin: Nǐmen dōu xǐhuān kàn diànyǐng ma?
u7-all-movies.meaning: Do you all like watching movies?
u7-all-movies.note: This is a yes/no question about everyone in the group, so use the familiar 嗎.

u7-photo-description.note: Describe the photo with 很好看, without 是.

u7-like-swim.note: 游泳 is one complete activity after 喜歡.

u7-weekend-often.meaning: I often swim on weekends. Start with “I.”
u7-weekend-often.note: Put the time before 常 and the activity after it.
